adaptations: Native capture returns bytes; the output matrix asserts original UTF-8 and newline bytes before Python universal-newline decoding, including both 200000-byte streams and nonzero exits.
Receipt parsing ports use the native version-2 header and pending/unit envelope so malformed-unit cases reach actual field validation instead of failing solely on missing headers.
Receipt cleanup contention uses a real DataLock held by another thread. The caller deadline now includes both receipt-read lock acquisitions.
Subprocess fixtures are compiled Rust programs linked against the current native core, with file rendezvous; no Python runtime or imported oracle is used.
Signal refusal/escalation tests invoke production recorded_tree::settle through feature-gated, thread-scoped Backend overrides, then restore real observation and clean the actual child tree.

Native parent monitoring is pollable in the server wait loop, avoiding a daemon watcher thread. Tests use the same Monitor API and real named parent/child processes; no parent PID environment mutation occurs in the test runner.

Original fixture-observation tests patch their own Python helper clock and liveness function; native equivalents preserve that fixture test type, route liveness through production identity::alive, verify every PID/token call, and use a virtual clock without terminating anything.

Native Linux group observation reads procfs without a ps subprocess. The source ps row-integrity matrix feeds equivalent rows to the production procfs parser, including malformed/zero-group/incomplete observations and zombie controls. No ps fallback implementation is invented just for tests.

Original HelperManager admission races port to the actual native Registry finite-start path: the per-profile decision protects in-flight admission before process birth, real Session/OwnedTree workers run at three controlled phases, shutdown reports unresolved IDs within one budget, and late starts prove cleanup before returning. No Python lifecycle state labels are invented.

Python stream-reader lifetime controls use actual Rust capture subprocesses and OS descriptor counts. A controlled cleanup refusal leaves the writer alive at acceptance; local pipe disposal is measured separately from retained process/Job handles and retry cleanup. Native capture has a single nonblocking reader and creates no reader threads. Same/separate inherited-writer cases exercise real trusted spawn receipts and capture BeforeCleanup, preserving trailing bytes and identified process-death checks before fixture rescue.

Unavailable lease observations use real filesystem obstructions at the directory/open stages, then repair and acquire the lease; native Registry status conservatively treats inaccessible or held leases as in use.

Native SDK ownership is explicit: Session publishes the exact tree claim before sending hello/open, independent of executable name, and no process-global Python spawn interception exists. Compiled native SDK transport fixtures create real browser descendants only on open; their disk record proves the claim existed before browser birth. Startup failures traverse the real Registry/Adapter APIs, and scheduled commits cannot run before successful context activation.

Camoufox body/close controls exercise the shared native SDK controller: real child/context protocol, original operation errors, cleanup refusal with a live browser and retained claim, then retry. Native release follows proved kernel-tree emptiness even when the vendor close response fails; a vendor cannot suppress ownership cleanup.

Claim IO faults use existing explicit vault::testing boundary observers at before-path-probe and before-claim-read, exercising real claim parsing/refusal while preserving original bytes. Inaccessible lease/claim stop scenarios use real filesystem obstructions and actual native CLI Profiles::stop plus Axum profile stop/status routes; unknown ownership never becomes a successful stopped result.

Current-profile race cases edit through the real repository at the explicit feature-gated post-lease admitted hook, then invoke actual native CLI launch/Registry launch, finite-probe, or scheduled-background paths. The SDK sees the post-lease profile, explicit engine overrides win, and both stored profile copies retain the concurrent edit.

Partial-reader construction faults port to actual native first/second pipe preparation and read boundaries, after a real OwnedTree spawn. The native architecture has no reader threads; tests measure OS handle disposal, actual reaping, and immutable returned Failure diagnostics after three real settlement retries. Adoption is explicit by construction; a post-spawn/pre-return fault and second-pipe fault cover the corresponding native failure boundaries.

Helper lifetime/overlap controls exercise the actual native Registry finite-owner table, Session leases and real worker processes. Shutdown overlap uses a controlled real signal boundary, a second caller blocked on the per-profile decision, and one terminal cleanup; its boolean reports which caller performed the stop, so [true,false] are two successful idempotent outcomes. Three surviving helpers verify one shared cleanup deadline, retained exact IDs, and successful real retry after injected refusal.

The shared thread/OS lock budget case uses a real OS lock held by a compiled child, a paused first local owner, and a second thread whose300ms deadline spans both waits. Wrong-thread release is rejected by the real Rust compiler because LockGuard is !Send, then a real external process proves that the acquiring thread retained its OS lock until normal guard drop.

Cross-process writes use compiled native child processes released together by file rendezvous, exercising real ProfileRepo, ProxyPool, ScheduleStore and vault migration transaction locks. The vault writer is held at the real before-migration boundary while another child enters a profile edit; final proof checks every encrypted stored credential and decrypted original value.

Unresolved/damaged receipt cases run isolated compiled native worker processes with real separately owned descendants holding output writers. They remove/corrupt actual version2 receipts after a trusted spawn, measure bounded failure and local descriptor closure before teardown, and retain evidence until explicit repair/retry. The leader control reaches actual EOF on both writers while the producer stays alive and cleanup is refused; its zero-unit receipt remains owned until producer-tree proof. No fixture rescue contributes to acceptance measurements.

Native finite capture has no pipe-reader threads. Original late-thread completion cases therefore exercise the actual SDK adapter I/O workers: the source stdout parameter holds the output reader after real EOF, and source stderr holds the native input writer after its pipe is closed. Context is captured explicitly into those real worker threads. Bounded finish fails while a worker remains held, preserves returned data/metadata, then a release permits successful idempotent retry; disposal retains join handles in the production quarantine instead of detaching them.

Launcher-death and orphan controls use compiled native Session launchers and independently identified real browser descendants. A raw launcher is hard-killed; POSIX keeps its captured group claimed while Windows kill-on-close Job semantics recover it. A separate negative control proves an unowned orphan survives and retains a real OS lock. Native child tree-awareness reads the already-published exact claim and checks actual getpgrp/IsProcessInJob membership before completing; no child needs an inherited plaintext ownership capability.

Remaining kernel cases execute the native detached supervisor/gate and real durable JobStore outcomes. Untyped interception and ctypes binding checks become explicit ownership/typed windows-sys lifetime checks. Windows create/assignment failures occur at real Job boundaries before resume; Unix missing birth identity is refused and reaped rather than publishing an unverified owner. Callback/report refusal waits for actual descendants before failing. Partial-output evidence comes from the actual streamed nonblocking capture pipe; panic disposal runs isolated and checks real descriptor counts.

Driver capture concurrency uses actual native per-root publication transactions and explicit Session capabilities, with independent profile preflight and exactly one activated owner. Invalid registry kind is rejected by rustc at the actual public API. HTTP shutdown tests launch a real native adapter/browser and inspect actual retained claims and kernel cleanup, including propagated shutdown refusal. Shell-death uses native_entry::dispatch, its actual Monitor/Server teardown, and browser/renderer OS locks. The original Python global socket-audit hook is replaced by an explicit scoped native socket fixture used by these real HTTP connections: it allocates a socket, checks policy before connect, and verifies closed OS handle after denial; loopback success is an in-case control.

Final native claim release rechecks kernel evidence within the same Session cleanup deadline; unknown observations are retried only while budget remains and never become empty by default. The existing closed-browser case injects one actual final-proof observation error after claim reading to exercise this retry. SessionLease Drop explicitly unlocks before closing so unrelated fork CLOEXEC copies cannot outlive the lease owner.

The exact source socket-denial case executes its explicit fixture scope in an isolated single-case native test child so sibling tests cannot reuse the just-closed descriptor before its actual kernel-closure check.
